description: Actual native 0.11 game screenshots for visual feedback: the Science window, eight live bubbles, Focused window and explicit navigation. Deterministic fixtures, not a real-time play recording or proof of physical-phone support.

screens.title: 01 · Welcome to Mars
screens.description: Opening story: the fictional year 2059 and Mars setting. Review the title, background contrast and first impression.

screens.title: 02 · Meet Ren
screens.description: The second story beat introduces the teammate outside. Review how quickly the picture and short text explain the situation.

screens.title: 03 · Your control room
screens.description: The final story beat introduces the player’s role before entering the control room.

screens.title: Opening the window
screens.description: Actual temporary loading state before the scene is built. Back to Home can cancel; mission time has not started.

screens.title: Ready to begin
screens.description: Unstarted Science window with the outpost frame, all eight live concept bubbles and three primary readings. The child can choose a cleaning pace and press Start without completing science cards.

screens.title: Cleaning in progress
screens.description: Actual mixed-pace fixture: 47.5% of the panel cleaned, 16% authored game fatigue and 48 active-play seconds remaining. Eight live science bubbles surround the outpost window; the pace control and Ren’s captions remain below.

screens.title: Choose your window
screens.description: The actual View menu pauses the mission. Science window is selected; the player can choose Focused window, resume, return to the menu, or open sound and motion settings.

screens.title: Focused window
screens.description: The same 47.5%-cleaned mission in Focused window mode. The panel and astronaut use a larger area; science remains available through the Science button. Changing views does not advance time or alter the model.

screens.title: The countdown is nearly over
screens.description: Actual mission with 0.3 active-play seconds remaining before automatic shelter entry. The storm is an authored game scenario.

screens.title: Explore science
screens.description: Optional eight-idea library with Radiation and Dust explored. Reading is not required to enter the mission.

screens.title: Microgray: the first explanation
screens.description: Concise concept view: a short definition, diagram and analogy. More explanation and source information expand separately.

screens.title: Power and stored energy
screens.description: The power concept explains the relationship between the production rate and accumulated energy.

screens.title: Science during play
screens.description: Opening Science pauses the active mission and exposes all eight discoveries. The displayed values come from the current run.

screens.title: A discovery opened during play
screens.description: Microgray opened from the paused discovery library. Back to Science names the actual return destination.

screens.title: NASA Sun image
screens.description: Offline fixture showing the explicitly labeled bundled NASA/SDO example image. This screenshot is not evidence of a fresh observation or a Mars forecast.

screens.title: NASA connection details
screens.description: The same offline NASA viewer with connection details expanded. Review source timestamps, image attribution and clarity of status.

screens.title: Take a break
screens.description: The actual paused mission menu provides explicit Resume, Science, View and accessibility, settings and leave/restart destinations. Pausing and reading do not consume mission time.

screens.title: Sound, motion and play time
screens.description: Settings opened from the paused mission menu. Sound, reduced motion and round length are separate choices; changing the real play duration preserves the simulated equations. Back returns to the originating menu.

screens.title: Settings opened from View
screens.description: Sound, motion and round-length settings opened from View while the mission is paused. Back returns to View; it does not silently resume play.

screens.title: Settings → View
screens.description: After pressing Back in settings opened from View, the actual View menu returns with Focused window still selected. The mission remains paused.

screens.title: Settings → mission menu
screens.description: After pressing Back in settings opened from the mission menu, that menu returns. The child can explicitly Resume mission or choose another destination.

screens.title: Mission result
screens.description: Actual completed mixed-pace run: 89.5% cleaned and Ren inside. Results appear immediately; all displayed scientific metrics come from the real model.

screens.title: Mission result · PASS
screens.description: An actual completed .5×-pace fixture: 46.875% cleaned, 1.703125 kWh stored and 10.9375 µGy model dose. Ren is inside; the game encourages more cleaning next time. The real model is advanced deterministically, not played in real time.

screens.title: Mission result · TRY AGAIN
screens.description: An actual completed .25×-pace fixture: 23.4375% cleaned, 1.3515625 kWh stored and 10.9375 µGy model dose. Ren is inside; the result invites a new cleaning plan. The real model is advanced deterministically, not played in real time.

screens.title: Eight ideas come together
screens.description: Actual science transition held at 0.35 seconds by the visual fixture. The game normally animates the ideas together; reduced motion skips this transition.

screens.title: How the science connects
screens.description: Four clickable visual relationships connect the eight ideas. Precise equations, numerical results and graphs remain available in optional detail.

screens.title: The numbers behind the result
screens.description: Expanded numerical explanations use the actual run’s generated energy, supplied energy and accumulated model dose.

screens.title: Your mission graphs
screens.description: Graphs are drawn from the actual recorded mission history. They show modeled stored energy and accumulated dose, not live NASA predictions.

screens.title: Try the idea somewhere new
screens.description: Optional transfer question after the completed mission. The first answer is retained when a learner tries again.

screens.title: Home
screens.description: The actual Home menu after the completed run: play, optional science, story, updates, View and accessibility, sound and motion settings, and More.

screens.title: Settings → Home
screens.description: After opening settings from Home and pressing Back, Home returns without starting or replacing a mission.

screens.title: More to explore
screens.description: Secondary Home destinations: settings, NASA observations, the earlier advanced lab and Quit.

screens.title: Updates & downloads · source-run mode
screens.description: The actual idle update interface opened from Home in an isolated source run. This mode explicitly says in-game installation is unavailable; no check, download or install was requested. This image does not establish packaged-host updater behavior.

screens.title: Small phone: opening story
screens.description: Actual 320×568 native viewport. Review title wrapping, contrast and reachable navigation at a small phone-shaped size.

screens.title: Phone: cleaning view
screens.description: Actual 390×844 native Science window during the same mixed-pace run. Eight live concepts use a horizontally scrollable rail above the framed work area. This verifies composition, not performance on a physical phone.

screens.title: Phone: Focused window
screens.description: Actual 390×844 native viewport in Focused window mode. Review the enlarged work area, three primary readings and reachable controls. This is composition evidence, not physical-phone performance.

screens.title: Small phone: cleaning view
screens.description: Actual 320×568 native Science window. The eight concepts remain reachable in a horizontally scrollable rail; the screenshot shows its starting position. Review the title, three readings, framed work area and pace controls.

screens.title: Small phone: choose your window
screens.description: Actual 320×568 native viewport showing the scrollable View menu. Review readable choices and access to Resume, Back and settings; this is not a physical mobile-device test.

screens.title: Small phone: results
screens.description: Actual 320×568 result screen. Review which result information is visible first and how the next actions are reached.

screens.title: Phone: science connections
screens.description: Actual 390×844 science page. Cards can scroll vertically; the science tokens remain actionable.

screens.title: Short landscape: cleaning view
screens.description: Actual 844×390 native Science window. All eight concept bubbles use compact side columns around the framed work area. Review Ren, the panel, readings and pace controls in a short landscape window.
